description: On startup, seeds the working rules file from the shipped default unless it already exists. On every session start, and whenever the data-directory rules file changes, narrows agents/ to the fleet agents those rules let anyone reach, watches that file, and asks each session for /reload-plugins when its set changed; an invalid rules or models file leaves agents/ as it is, and a session with FLEET_RULES set leaves agents/ to the data-directory file. Before every Agent, Skill, Workflow and Bash call, identifies the caller: the main session's Agent calls are checked against the main section and its other calls pass; a fleet subagent's Agent calls are checked against its row in rules, its Skill and Bash calls against the disallowed lists, and its Workflow calls are refused; a fleet agent type is recognised by its definition or, when that file is gone, by its name in models.json, and one carrying the fleet prefix that neither resolves is refused; built-in subagents pass. A rules file that is not exactly one JSON object (an empty file, several documents, a top-level array or string, text that is not JSON; null reads as empty rules) makes these checks refuse. When a fleet agent starts, the same guard hands it the disallowed skills and commands, so it does not try them; a refused skill is not a reason to stop. Separately, an Agent call that targets a fleet agent is refused unless its prompt is a structured brief with the required sections; calls to other agent types are not inspected.
